Naomi Osaka. A Japanese-Haitian tennis champion who won four Grand Slam singles titles and became a global icon for her outspoken advocacy on mental health and social justice. Her powerful serve and baseline game established her as one of the leading players of the 2020s, with a legacy extending far beyond tennis into activism. She won two Australian Opens in 2019 and 2021, and two US Opens in 2018 and 2020. She rose to world number one in 2019 at age twenty-one, the first player from Japan, male or female, to reach the top ranking and win a Grand Slam title. Known for her powerful serve and aggressive forehand, her athletic ability and mental toughness enabled her to compete at the highest levels from an early age. In 2021 she took a break from professional tennis to focus on mental health, candidly discussing depression and anxiety in a pioneering move that helped normalize mental health conversations in elite sports. She won the US Open final against Serena Williams in 2018 at age twenty, announcing herself as a future champion in a dramatic debut against one of tennis's greatest players. Her activism extends to racial justice and social causes beyond tennis, and she represents a new generation of athletes using their platform and influence for advocacy and social change.
